title: Ask the person a question
hook: Make programs that ask, then work with the answer.

warmup.explain: 17 divided by 5 is 3 whole times with 2 left over. `%` gives the leftover.

warmup.q: Which of these is a good variable name?
warmup.explain: No spaces and never start with a number. Underscores are fine.

warmup.q: Which of these is text, not a number?
warmup.explain: Anything inside quotes is text, even if it looks like a number.

why.heading: Programs that ask
why.text:
Until now you typed every value into the code. `input` makes the program pause, show a question, and wait for someone to type:

`name = input("Name? ")`

Whatever they type is stored in `name`. Put a space at the end of the question so the answer does not touch it.

why.heading: Why it matters
why.text:
With `input`, one program works for anyone. Any crew member's hours, any runner's distance. You write it once and the answers change each run.

That is the difference between a note and a tool.

why.heading: input is always text
why.text:
Even when someone types 6, `input` gives you the text `"6"`. Yesterday you saw that text is not a number: `"6" * 2` gives `66`, not 12.

So before doing sums with an answer, you must convert it.

why.heading: Convert it
why.text:
`int("6")` turns text into a whole number. `float("5.5")` turns it into a decimal. `str(6)` turns a number back into text.

You can ask and convert in one line:

`hours = int(input("Hours? "))`

why.heading: When it cannot convert
why.text: `int("seven")` fails, because seven is not digits. Python shows a **ValueError**. That is not a bug in your lines: the person typed something the program could not turn into a number. Later in the course you will learn to handle that politely.

watch.intro: Tap Run. The answers (Thabo and 6) are typed for you, like a real session.
watch.code:
name = input("Name? ")
hours = int(input("Hours? "))
print(f"{name} worked {hours} hours")
print(f"Double time: {hours * 2}")
explain: Line 1 asks, waits, and stores the text typed.
Line 2 asks and converts to a whole number in one go.
Because `hours` is now an int, `hours * 2` is a real sum (12).
watch.break_it: Break it on purpose: change line 2 to `hours = int("seven")` and tap Run. The error says `ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: 'seven'`. That is what you will see whenever text cannot become a number. Put line 2 back.

tasks.title: Greet the crew
tasks.task:
Ask for a name, then greet them. For the answer `Sam` the screen shows:

`Name? Sam`
`Hello, Sam`
tasks.starter:
name = input("Name? ")
# print Hello, then the name
hints: The answer is already stored in name. Now print it.

tasks.title: Day rate total
tasks.task:
The day rate is R2500. Ask how many days were worked, convert the answer to a whole number, and print the total. For `3` days:

`Days? 3`
`Total: R7500`
tasks.starter:
days = input("Days? ")
rate = 2500
# convert days to an int, then print the total
tasks.solution:
days = input("Days? ")
rate = 2500
days = int(days)
print(f"Total: R{days * rate}")
hints: days is text. Turn it into a number first: days = int(days)
Then multiply days by rate inside an f-string.

tasks.title: Pace from your run
tasks.task:
Ask for kilometres, then minutes (both can have decimals, so use float). Print the pace with 2 decimals. For 5 and 28:

`Km? 5`
`Minutes? 28`
`Pace: 5.60 min/km`
tasks.starter:
km = input("Km? ")
mins = input("Minutes? ")
# convert both to float, then print the pace
tasks.solution:
km = float(input("Km? "))
mins = float(input("Minutes? "))
print(f"Pace: {mins / km:.2f} min/km")
hints: Wrap each input in float(...) so you can do maths with it.
Pace is minutes divided by km. Use :.2f for two decimals.

recap: `input("question ")` pauses, asks, and gives back what was typed.
`input` always gives text, even for digits.
`int()` and `float()` turn text into numbers. `str()` turns a number into text.
`int("seven")` gives a ValueError: it is not a number.

words.meaning: Asks the person a question and returns their answer as text.
Turn one kind of value into another.
Turns text into a whole number.
Turns text into a decimal number.
The value could not be turned into what you asked for.
